summary.oneLiner: Jindal Steel completed a transformative capacity expansion to 15.6 MTPA in FY26, driving volume growth but compressing per-tonne EBITDA due to startup costs and coking coal inflation. The key inflection point is FY27, where the commissioning of the slurry pipeline (INR 750-1,000/tonne savings) and stabilization of the new Angul assets are expected to restore margins despite a strategic shift toward lower-margin flat products.
summary.business: Jindal Steel is an integrated steel producer with backward integration into captive iron ore mining and forward integration into rolling and downstream processing, manufacturing a wide range of long steel products and specialised plate solutions. Its products serve defence and shipbuilding, railways, construction and infrastructure, energy (wind, hydro, thermal), oil and gas, general engineering and OEM customers, alongside a retail rebar brand for individual home builders. The company sells predominantly in the domestic market across 28 states and also exports to more than 35 countries.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated value chain from captive raw materials (iron ore mines at Kasia, Tensa and Roida-I; non-coking and coking coal capacities) through iron making, steelmaking, rolling and downstream processing|India's largest technologically advanced Hot Strip Mill with 6 MTPA annual production capacity|Strategically located five-site manufacturing footprint (Raigarh, Raipur, Angul, Barbil, Patratu) supporting logistics and cost competitiveness|Diversified, value-added product portfolio spanning long and flat/plate products serving strategic sectors including defence, railways and infrastructure|Established retail distribution network under the JINDAL PANTHER brand alongside a predominantly B2B/institutional customer base|Post year-end credit rating upgrade (CARE AA to AA+, Stable) reflecting strengthening balance sheet and credit profile
currentContext.strategies: Scaling for the next phase of growth by leveraging the larger, integrated manufacturing platform at Angul (emerging as one of the world's largest single-location steel plants) to increase volumes, expand value-added offerings and enhance operating efficiencies|Strengthening raw material security through strategic investments in iron ore and coal assets to enhance self-sufficiency, reduce exposure to market volatility and improve cost competitiveness|Driving growth through value-added products by increasing focus on specialised and value-added products and investing in flat products and downstream facilities to expand into automotive, engineering, infrastructure and construction segments|Building structural cost advantages via infrastructure investments (slurry pipeline, dedicated port infrastructure, surplus captive power capacity) to reduce logistics costs and support margin sustainability|Maintaining strong cash generation and financial discipline to fund one of the largest expansion programmes in the Company's history while preserving a resilient balance sheet|Embedding sustainability into the growth journey, with a Net Zero ambition by 2047, a target to cut CO2 emissions intensity, coal gasification and slurry pipeline projects for resource efficiency, and a 'Zero Harm' safety philosophy backed by strengthened ESG governance|The Company manages financial capital through disciplined capital allocation, prudent risk management and a focus on operational performance, seeking to balance growth, profitability and financial resilience as market conditions evolve. Cash generation, liquidity and balance-sheet capacity are directed to support investment in capacity expansion, asset modernisation and other projects intended to strengthen long-term competitiveness, and also to support sustainability and decarbonisation priorities such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, resource productivity and low-carbon technologies. On dividends, the Board has framed a Dividend Distribution Policy under SEBI Listing Regulations that establishes the parameters considered before declaring or recommending a dividend, and has recommended a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share (face value Rs 1) for FY 2025-26; no amount was transferred to reserves during the year.
currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 marked the successful completion of Phase II of the Angul Integrated Steel Plant, taking installed crude steelmaking capacity to 15.6 MTPA (12.0 MTPA at Angul and 3.6 MTPA at Raigarh). During the year the Company commissioned the 4.6 MTPA Blast Furnace 'Bhagavati Subhadrika', 3.0 MTPA BOF-2 and 3.0 MTPA BOF-3, operationalised both modules of the Shree Bhoomi Power Plant (2 x 525 MW), commissioned a 1.2 MTPA Cold Rolling Mill complex, and completed the pipe conveyor system connecting the Utkal mines with the Angul steel plant. The 192-km Barbil-Angul slurry pipeline is nearing completion, expected to reduce transportation dependency, logistics costs and emissions once operational. Development of the Paradip Port berth is continuing, with commissioning and ramp-up planned in a phased manner from FY 2026-27 onwards. As of March 31, 2026, the Company had incurred cumulative capital expenditure of Rs 35,498 crore out of a total planned investment of Rs 47,043 crore for its integrated expansion programme, with the remaining capex expected to support completion, integration and ramp-up of ongoing projects. On raw materials, the Company progressed the Thakurani-A1 and Roida-I iron ore blocks and the Saradhapur Jalatap East and Utkal B1 coal blocks to strengthen captive resource security alongside its existing Kasia, Tensa, Gare Palma IV/6 and Utkal C assets. Separately, in the overseas coal portfolio, the Company reassessed its Australian mine (previously under care and maintenance) and, given the mining shaft has been sealed, recognised a non-cash impairment reflecting a prudent reassessment of recoverable value; its Mozambique and South Africa operations remained stable with no material change in structure.

risks.risk: Impaired/stranded overseas coking coal asset in Australia
risks.note: The Australian mine remained non-operational and under care and maintenance during FY 2025-26; a comprehensive reassessment found the mining shaft has been sealed, and the Company recognised a non-cash impairment charge reflecting the reassessment of the asset's recoverable value in line with current operational realities.

risks.risk: Loss-making South Africa operations amid a high-cost environment
risks.note: South Africa operations faced subdued market conditions, operational constraints and a high cost environment during FY 2025-26; anthracite coal production fell sharply year-on-year and both EBITDA and PAT remained negative and widened versus the prior year, with the Company still evaluating operational improvements and cost optimisation to sustain the asset long-term.

risks.risk: Commodity and energy price volatility driven by geopolitical shocks
risks.note: Brent crude swung sharply in early CY2026 (to around US$120/bbl in April 2026 from US$69/bbl average in CY2025) following Middle East conflict and disruption risk to the Strait of Hormuz, illustrating the Company's exposure to volatile input/energy costs and shipping-route disruption beyond its control.

risks.risk: Dependence on trade-protection measures against Chinese steel overcapacity
risks.note: Domestic price realisations and import competition remain tied to the continuation of the 12% safeguard duty on select steel imports (in force till April 2028); persistent global overcapacity, particularly from China, and evolving tariff/non-tariff barriers globally keep international trade flows and Indian steel pricing exposed to policy shifts.

risks.risk: Rising finance costs pressuring standalone interest coverage
risks.note: The standalone Interest Coverage Ratio declined versus the prior year due to a decrease in EBITDA and an increase in net finance charges during the year ended 31 March 2026, alongside a decline in standalone Operating Margin and Net Profit Margin, indicating margin and debt-servicing headroom is narrowing even as the balance sheet funds a large expansion programme.

The Risk Management Committee's charter specifically calls out cyber security as a particular area of risk assessment, monitoring and review, reflecting the Company's exposure to cyber threats across its integrated, multi-site manufacturing and IT/OT operations.

risks.risk: Operational complexity of global operations across multiple geographies
risks.note: The Company operates raw-material and coal assets across India, Mozambique, South Africa and Australia; performance has diverged sharply by geography (e.g., Mozambique improved while South Africa and Australia weakened/impaired), exposing consolidated results to country-specific operational, cost and regulatory conditions.

one-line thesis: Jindal Steel completed a transformative capacity expansion to 15.6 MTPA in FY26, driving volume growth but compressing per-tonne EBITDA due to startup costs and coking coal inflation. The key inflection point is FY27, where the commissioning of the slurry pipeline (INR 750-1,000/tonne savings) and stabilization of the new Angul assets are expected to restore margins despite a strategic shift toward lower-margin flat products.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 62,412 Cr (+8% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 19,399 Cr (+28% QoQ). EBITDA: INR 9,099 Cr (FY26), INR 10,482/tonne (vs INR 11,712/tonne FY25); Q4 Adj EBITDA INR 2,647 Cr (INR 10,093/tonne). PAT: INR 3,361 Cr (+18% YoY); Q4 PAT INR 1,041 Cr. Order Book: Not explicitly quantified, but sales mix 52% flat/48% long in Q4. Net Debt: INR 16,019 Cr (1.66x Net Debt/EBITDA). One-offs: INR 1,433 Cr impairment (Standalone) / INR 834 Cr (Consolidated) on Australian assets; INR 125 Cr startup costs in Q4 (now complete).
guidance: FY27 Production: 11.0-11.5 MTPA; Sales: 10.5-11.0 MTPA. Margins: No specific % guidance, but expects normalization by Q2FY27; Coking coal cost headwind of $20-25/tonne in Q1FY27. Order Inflow: Focused on infrastructure/longs transitioning to flats. Capex: Remaining INR 11,545 Cr of total INR 47,043 Cr program; FY27 sustenance/expansion capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 Cr.
order book & pipeline: Sales volume Q4: 2.62 MT (+23% YoY, +15% QoQ). Product Mix Q4: 52% Flat, 48% Longs (vs 49% Flat, 51% Longs for FY26). Target mix shifting to ~70% Flats over time. Realization: Blended ASP up INR 4,743/tonne QoQ in Q4.
segment / subsidiary detail: Angul expansion operational (BF2 4.6 MT, BOF2/3 3 MT each). Cold Rolling Complex (1.2 MT) enhancing value add. Power: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi plant commissioned. Mining: Thakurani-A1 iron ore block (preferred bidder); Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded. Australian mine (Wollongong) shaft closed, reserves inaccessible.
growth verticals / optionality: Slurry pipeline (Barbil-Angul) commissioning Q1FY27 (est. INR 750-1,000/tonne steel-level savings). DRI-2 and PP2 commissioning towards end of FY27. Port facilities commissioning soon. Cross-selling expanded flat portfolio to existing infrastructure customers.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA/tonne pressured by coking coal hike ($20/tonne) and startup costs (INR 125 Cr total in Q4). Slurry pipeline expected to offset raw material inflation partially. Shift to flats (lower margin than longs) is a structural mix headwind, mitigated by value-added grades in HRC/Plates.
capex / expansion: Total program INR 47,043 Cr; Invested INR 35,498 Cr by end-FY26. Remaining INR 11,545 Cr. FY27 allocation INR 7,500-10,000 Cr focused on sustenance and final commissioning (DRI-2, PP2, Slurry).
capital allocation: Debt reduction priority (leverage to normalize by Q2FY27). Final dividend INR 2/share. No major M&A; focus on 'asset sweating' post-capex cycle. Internal accruals funded ~75% of recent capex surge.
risks & watch-items: Coking coal price volatility (Q1 headwind guided). Delay in slurry pipeline or DRI-2 commissioning. Global steel oversupply (China exports). Execution risk in shifting mix to 70% flats without approval delays. Further impairments ruled out for Australia.
management quality / tone: Confident on volume ramp-up and market demand (9%+ India growth); Pragmatic on margin compression due to mix/costs; Decisive on writing off Australian assets to clean up balance sheet; Focused on operational efficiency ('asset sweating').
non-obvious takeaways: The impairment of the Australian asset is final with no further cash outflow expected, yet the license is retained. The shift to 70% flat products is a deliberate strategic pivot to become a 'one-stop shop' for infrastructure clients, accepting lower per-tonne margins for higher absolute volume and stickiness. The slurry pipeline savings are per-tonne of steel produced, not just iron ore transported, amplifying the EBITDA impact.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
